newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SPRING/WHITE WHEAT - BIDS DECLINE.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SPRING/WHITE WHEAT - BIDS DECLINE.

text.p: Dark northern spring wheat and soft white wheat bids fell on Monday, dealers said.
Montana dealers cited harvest progress in winter wheat but noted that many elevators were close to full.
In southern Montana, some of the bigger farms were 50 percent done with the winter wheat harvest and were just getting started with spring wheat, a grain merchandiser said.

But the smaller farms have not started harvesting their winter wheat yet. "It will be a long harvest. We are yielding around 50 bushels per acre for winter wheat" up from the norm of about 30 to 35 bushels per acre, the dealer said.

The dealer noted a lack of storage place for the wheat in southern Montana. "There is so much wheat that the farmer has no where to store it." Many elevators in Billings andose to full, the dealer said.
"If we could get more trains to come out here we would not have this problem," the dealer said. "Yellowstone and Bighorn counties are the problematic areas where they have a lot of grain."
"By the end of August and 1st of September we should get some of the pressure off of us if we get a couple of more trains loaded," the dealer added.
But another Montana dealer said his area had enough onfarm storage space for grain.
